statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the number of ordered pairs (a,b) such that a occurs as a value in nums, b occurs as a value in nums, and pc(a OR b) + pc(a AND b) >= k. Here pc(x) is the number of set bits in the binary representation of x. Pairs are ordered: (a,b) and (b,a) are distinct when a != b, while (a,a) is included exactly once for each value a that occurs in nums. Multiplicities in nums are ignored: a value occurring one or more times is available once as a possible component value. Equivalently, because pc(a OR b) + pc(a AND b) = pc(a) + pc(b) for nonnegative a and b, the condition is pc(a) + pc(b) >= k.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: The function returns a result (it does not fail, overflow, panic, or access outside the slice) for every input satisfying the preconditions; in particular, the returned value is a valid 64-bit signed integer.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= 0.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= d*d, where d is the number of distinct values occurring in nums.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums and let m = min {pc(v) | v in D}. For any input satisfying the preconditions, if k <= 2*m, then whenever the function returns a result r, r = d*d, where d = |D|.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums and let M = max {pc(v) | v in D}. For any input satisfying the preconditions, if k > 2*M, then whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: If all entries of nums are equal to a single value v (that is, nums[i] = v for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)), then whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if 2*pc(v) >= k and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums and D2 the set of distinct values occurring in nums2. If D = D2, then whenever count_excellent_pairs(nums,k) returns r and count_excellent_pairs(nums2,k) returns r2, we have r = r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices each satisfying: len at least 1 and at most 100000; every element between 1 and 1000000000; and 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums and D2 the set of distinct values occurring in nums2. If D is a subset of D2, then whenever count_excellent_pairs(nums,k) returns r and count_excellent_pairs(nums2,k) returns r2, we have r <= r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices each satisfying: len at least 1 and at most 100000; every element between 1 and 1000000000; and 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Whenever count_excellent_pairs(nums,k1) returns r1 and count_excellent_pairs(nums,k2) returns r2, we have r2 <= r1.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 60.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums, and let h be the number of v in D such that 2*pc(v) >= k. Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= h*h.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums. Let d_eq be the number of v in D with 2*pc(v) >= k. Let d_neq be the number of unordered two-element subsets {a,b} of D (so a != b) such that pc(a)+pc(b) >= k. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = d_eq + 2*d_neq.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every value a occurring in nums and every value b occurring in nums, pc(a OR b) + pc(a AND b) < k (equivalently pc(a)+pc(b) < k).
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Let c_t be the number of distinct values v occurring in nums with pc(v) = t, for t = 0..63. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = sum over all pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i <= 63, 0 <= j <= 63 and i + j >= k of c_i * c_j.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums and D2 the set of distinct values occurring in nums2. If the multisets of popcounts {pc(v) | v in D} and {pc(v) | v in D2} are equal, then whenever count_excellent_pairs(nums,k) returns r and count_excellent_pairs(nums2,k) returns r2, we have r = r2.
preconditions: nums and nums2 are slices each satisfying: len at least 1 and at most 100000; every element between 1 and 1000000000; and the same k with 1 <= k <= 60.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct values occurring in nums, let d = |D| and let m = min {pc(v) | v in D}. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = d*d if and only if k <= 2*m.
preconditions: len(nums) is at least 1 and at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; 1 <= k <= 60.
